explain.say: After a long bath or swim, your fingertips look like little raisins. But why only fingers and toes, and not your nose? Look at the hand on the board. After about five minutes in water, nerves in your fingertips notice that the skin is wet.

faq.q: Why do fingers wrinkle in water?
faq.a: Nerves sense that your skin is wet and make tiny blood vessels under the fingertips narrow. With less filling underneath, the skin folds into wrinkles.
asks: Why do my fingers go pruney in the bath?

faq.q: How long does it take for fingers to wrinkle?
faq.a: Wrinkles start after about five minutes in warm water and get deeper over about half an hour.
asks: When do fingers start to wrinkle?

faq.q: Do wrinkly fingers help you grip?
faq.a: Possibly. A 2013 study found people with wrinkled fingers handled wet objects faster, like tyre treads draining water, but other studies have not all agreed.

faq.q: Why don't other parts of my body wrinkle in water?
faq.a: Fingertips and toes have thick skin and many nerve-controlled blood vessels, so they react the most. Other skin barely changes.
asks: Why doesn't my face wrinkle in the bath?

faq.a: Yes. Once you dry off, the blood vessels relax and your skin smooths out within minutes.
asks: How long do wrinkly fingers last?

facts: Fingers whose nerves have been cut do not wrinkle in water, showing that the nervous system controls the wrinkling.
Water wrinkles on the fingers usually start after about five minutes of soaking.
